next_step: Kickoff infra + networking for Dedicated POC; finalize SOW and pricing; schedule canary run
notes: Inbound from product team (VP Product) - seeking in-app generative features: contextual chat + document search for enterprise customers.
Initial trial on Hosted API (Oct-Nov): tried redwood-recommended 13B (standard) and 7B quantized for cost comparison. Quality acceptable, latency varied between regions.
Decision path: start with Hosted for rapid feature launch, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit costs once traffic stabilizes.
POC ask: 6-week Dedicated pilot with canary rollout (5% -> 20% -> 100%) and explicit fallback routing plan (model and region).

Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for typical UI flows (short chat turns), burst throughput target: 150-250 req/s. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to trade some latency for >2x cost reduction vs Hosted at scale.

Model preferences: prefer open-model variants. Evaluated: redwood-13b-v1 (higher quality) and redwood-7b-q4 (quantized cheaper). Want guidance on quantization/FP16 tradeoffs for conversation length up to 1024 tokens.

Security: require SSO (SAML), KMS integration for key management, VPC peering to GCP project, retention controls for conversation logs (30d default, opt-in extended retention), and audit logging to central SIEM.
Quote & pricing discussion in Drive (pricing_and_sow_skyward). AE pushed draft committed capacity model with 2x A100-equivalent baseline and burst buffer.

Customer explicitly asked: 'How do you handle region failover and model rollback without user-visible regressions?' - we proposed canary + automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant and fallback to alternate region with cached KV prefixes.
Internal: SE (Liam) to run a micro-benchmark comparing tail-latency under continuous batching vs naive synchronous calls. CSM (Nina) prepping SLO expectations and onboarding checklist.
Quote from VP Eng on 11/29 call: 'We need the canary to prove no more than 1% quality delta vs Hosted baseline; otherwise we won't flip 100% traffic.'
